issues.description: The UML diagram and problem statement declare Pneumatic.openValve() as a no-argument method, but the solution's Pneumatic interface declares openValve(int duration). At the same time, the solution's implementing classes (LaunchedRollerCoaster and LaunchedDropdownTower) implement openValve() with no parameters. This signature mismatch between the Pneumatic interface and its implementations (and between the solution and the UML/problem statement) will cause compilation errors and confuses students which signature to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Pneumatic.openValve signature across artifacts. The simplest fix preserving the UML/problem intent is to change the solution's Pneumatic interface to declare void openValve() (no parameters). Alternatively, if an int parameter is intended, update the UML/problem statement and all implementing classes to accept the same int parameter. Preferred: modify src/de/tum/in/ase/Pneumatic.java to declare void openValve().
